findings.title: Attention Factors for Statistical Arbitrage
findings.summary: Learns conditional latent factors from firm-characteristic embeddings via attention, jointly optimized with the trading strategy instead of a separate cointegration/distance pair-selection step. Backtest: largest US equities, 24yr period, gross Sharpe >4, net 2.3 after costs.
findings.reason_not_staged: Already in wiki/trading/algorithms/pairs-trading.md ('Key Insight: Weak Factors Matter' section, Net OOS Sharpe 2.3) -- confirmed via grep before drafting a proposal. Not a duplicate scan error; the paper was independently found again tonight but was already ingested (date of original ingest not confirmed, predates tonight).

findings.title: Statistical arbitrage in multi-pair trading via graph clustering algorithms in US equities
findings.summary: Uses graph clustering (not correlation/cointegration screening) to form candidate pairs, ML classifier ensemble filters signals, novel time-varying stop-loss/Kelly sizing.
findings.reason_not_staged: Predates the 2025-2026 preference window (June 2024) and no Sharpe/return numbers surfaced from the abstract-level fetch; below staging bar without concrete evidence.

findings.title: Hierarchical Deep Learning Framework for Pair Trading with Attention and Graph Networks
findings.summary: GAT-based pair selection layer + DRL execution layer, DRL performance as supervisory signal for the selector.
findings.reason_not_staged: No arXiv preprint, publisher-paywalled, no numbers accessible.

angles.angle_summary: No new HIGH-relevance finding beyond what's already logged. Best candidate (Attention Factors, 2510.11616) turned out to already be in pairs-trading.md. No new cointegration-test-statistic paper found beyond the already-known copula literature.

angles.angle: 2. arXiv: PEAD + post-earnings drift + text signals

findings.title: From Text to Alpha: Can LLMs Track Evolving Signals in Corporate Disclosures?
findings.summary: Embedding-based semantic drift in disclosed-metric emphasis quarter-over-quarter (not single-document sentiment). >2x risk-adjusted alpha vs. NER baseline, S&P 100 2010-2024.
findings.reason_not_staged: Already in wiki (nlp-alternative-data.md and hypothesis-log.md reference arXiv:2510.03195) -- confirmed via grep.

findings.title: The Language of Evasion: How Semantic Similarity Between Questions and Answers Predicts Stock Returns
findings.summary: LLM-embedding cosine similarity between analyst Q&A pairs on earnings calls as a directness/evasion signal, validated against 1,642 human-labeled pairs; 3.9% annual alpha for direct-answer executives.

findings.title: Enhancing Post Earnings Announcement Drift Measurement with Large Language Models
findings.summary: Compares BART vs FinBERT, tests adding pre-announcement price signals to text classification. FinBERT text-only 57.6-58.3% accuracy.
findings.reason_not_staged: Close to the already-rejected H317 multi-modal combo pattern; PDF extraction failed so multi-signal benefit vs. FinBERT-alone could not be confirmed.

findings.title: PEAD.txt / 'sentiment surprise' earnings-call NLP (QuantPedia writeup)
findings.summary: Signal = deviation of current-call sentiment from firm's own trailing-quarter sentiment mean (not absolute level), split by call section. Optimized variant CAGR 5.89%, Sharpe 0.76.
findings.reason_not_staged: Sharpe well below H174's live gate; built on earnings-call transcripts, same coverage-bias risk H168 already found fatal. 'Surprise relative to own history' framing noted as a genuinely different signal-design idea even though this specific implementation is weak -- worth remembering if a future transcript-coverage fix is found.

findings.title: FinCall-Surprise: A Large-Scale Multi-modal Benchmark for Earning Surprise Prediction
findings.summary: Eval benchmark adding audio/visual modalities from earnings calls; no strategy-level Sharpe disclosed.
findings.reason_not_staged: Benchmark not a strategy; infeasible near-term (no audio/video pipeline).

findings.title: FinAnchor: Aligned Multi-Model Representations for Financial Prediction
findings.summary: Aligns LLM text embeddings with tabular financial features into a unified representation space.
findings.reason_not_staged: No disclosed backtest numbers in accessible excerpt; underspecified for implementation.

angles.angle_summary: One genuinely new, well-evidenced, differentiated finding staged (Language of Evasion). Best other candidate (From Text to Alpha) already in wiki. Field-level observation: the frontier has moved from 'better single-document sentiment' (FinBERT successors -- none found) to 'cross-document/temporal or dialogue-structure signals' -- noted in the staged proposal's rationale.

findings.title: Revisiting Factor Momentum: A One-month Lag Perspective
findings.summary: Momentum-of-factor-returns (not stock returns) using a 1-month formation window instead of standard 12-month; significant alpha, robust to established factors.
findings.reason_not_staged: Conceptually distinct angle (rotate H026/H041a/H045/H198 sleeves by their own recent momentum -- related to the already-PROPOSED H318 meta-agent rotation idea) but paywalled (SSRN/journal, not free arXiv) with no disclosed Sharpe/return numbers to evaluate against the staging bar. Logged here so it isn't lost, but not actionable without the full methodology.

findings.title: Machine Learning Enhanced Multi-Factor Quantitative Trading (tradability masking)
findings.summary: Mask-first tradability filter preventing limit-move/suspension contamination of rolling-window factor calcs, A-share specific (+-10%/+-20% price limits).
findings.reason_not_staged: Problem (limit-up/down contamination) doesn't apply to US large-cap universe already used.

findings.title: Winners vs. Losers -- ESG regime-switching momentum
findings.summary: State-dependent long-short momentum via Bellman equation across ESG sentiment regimes.
findings.reason_not_staged: Long-short construction is exactly the leg already rejected in H243/H271 (short side loses on our universe).

findings.title: Refining and Robust Backtesting of a Century of Profitable Industry Trends
findings.summary: 100-year industry-momentum backtest; paper's own conclusion is that it fails to hold up on modern data after rigorous walk-forward testing.
findings.reason_not_staged: Negative result, pre-2025 window.

angles.angle_summary: No HIGH-relevance staged finding -- effectively a 'nothing materially new' result for this angle, consistent with how thoroughly the momentum family has already been explored (H198/H241/H243/H271/H291/H313/H336/H337/H341/H417/H418/H435-437). The two established momentum-crash fixes (Barroso-Santa-Clara vol-scaling, Daniel-Moskowitz dynamic momentum) remain state of the art; nothing found supersedes them. Transformer/attention-based cross-sectional rankers surfaced during the scan overlap with the already-ingested spatio-temporal-momentum-2023.md (arXiv:2302.10175) family rather than extending it, and were not separately reported.

findings.title: TradingAgents
findings.summary: Full trading-firm simulation: analyst agents -> bull/bear researcher debate -> trader -> 3-profile risk-team second debate -> fund-manager finalizer. Backtest (AAPL/GOOGL/AMZN, Jan-Mar 2024): Sharpe 5.60-8.21 vs best baseline 3.53.
findings.reason_not_staged: Already in wiki/trading/algorithms/multi-agent-llm-trading.md -- confirmed via grep.

findings.title: LLM-Powered Multi-Agent System for Automated Crypto Portfolio Management
findings.summary: 3 modality-specialized agents (Crypto/News/Trading), ablates hierarchical vs collaborative vs debate topologies x 4 capability configs. Best: Hierarchical+Skill, 133.52% cumulative return, Sharpe 1.502, top-15 L1 tokens 2025.
findings.reason_not_staged: Genuinely not yet in wiki (grep confirmed no match), but crypto-specific -- crypto momentum family (H302/H303) is already NOT CONFIRMED and deprioritized on this pipeline; the topology ablation (hierarchical beats debate/collaborative) is the one transferable insight, noted here rather than staged as a full proposal given the crypto mismatch.

findings.title: RAPTOR: Reasoned Agentic Portfolio Trading with Orchestrated Rebalancing
findings.summary: Per-asset agent debate feeds a Black-Litterman optimizer as investor-views input, blended with equilibrium priors -- aggregation-layer pattern distinct from H274/TradingAgents' facilitator-picks-a-thesis pattern.

findings.title: Toward Expert Investment Teams: Fine-Grained Trading Tasks
findings.summary: Argues fine-grained task decomposition beats coarse-grained analyst/manager role mimicry; tested on Japanese equities.
findings.reason_not_staged: Already in wiki/trading/algorithms/multi-agent-llm-trading.md ('Fine-Grained Task Decomposition' section) -- confirmed via grep.

findings.title: Agentic Trading survey (reproducibility audit)
findings.summary: Reproducibility audit finding only 2/19 studies in the space are reproducible.
findings.reason_not_staged: Useful caveat context for evaluating all other multi-agent claims (including tonight's), not itself an architecture or finding to stage.
